text: 1098T Tax Form | Brooklyn College 1098T Tax Form What Is a 1098T Tax Form? The IRS 1098T Tax Form is the tuition statement that indicates the total amount paid for tuition and fees for the entire calendar year. Who Is Eligible to Receive This Form? Students who make out-of-pocket payments toward their tuition for a particular calendar year are eligible to receive a 1098T form. However, you will not be eligible for a 1098-T for a particular calendar year if you have: received grants, scholarships, or third-party payments that meet or exceed your total tuition amount for the entire calendar year, or made payments during a different calendar year. How Can I Access My 1098T Form? You may access and print your 1098T form directly from your CUNYfirst account by following these steps: Log in to CUNYfirst Select Student Center. Select Financial Account tile. Select 1098T in the available menu (ensure your pop-up blocker for the CUNYfirst site is disabled to allow the report to appear). If you do not see the year for the form you are looking for, you may not be eligible for a 1098T Form for that year (see eligibility information above). Brooklyn. All in. Apply Now Contact Us

text: Tax Information | Hunter College Tax Information 529 Plan The NY State SAVES 529 program, as well as other similar state programs, are accepted by Hunter College as a means to pay for a student’s tuition and fee charges. Students are required to provide documentation of the exact amount being funded through the 529 program at least one week prior to the bill due date to allow time for processing. Please see the third party billing page for additional information. If the College bills the 529 program and fails to receive payment, the student will be held responsible for settling the bill. It is advised the student check with the program to ensure timely payment. 1098T Tax Form The 1098T tax form is issued to all Hunter students who pay tuition and fees from January 1 to December 31 of each calendar year. Forms are mailed by the CUNY l098T Server on January 31st of each year for the prior calendar year. You can access your 1098T by logging into CUNYfirst and following these steps: Click on Student Center Click on Financial Account Click View 1098T Students requesting duplicate 1098T forms for any years prior to the current year will be charged $5.00 per year. If you have a specific question about your 1098T form, please email Irving Rodriguez at irrodrig@hunter.cuny.edu . 1098T Form Tax Links IRS Information NACUBO Helpful Information NASFAA Helpful Information 1098T FAQs What expenses are not included on the form? Room and board or similar living expenses. Transportation. Meals. Books. Family expenses. Courses taken for no credit (unless taken to improve job skills). Expenses paid at any time other than in the current year for the current calendar year. Will I get a 1098T form if financial aid covered my tuition and fee charges? No. However, if financial aid covered only one semester in the current year, you will receive a form. Are direct loans included in my 1098T form? Yes, all monies you must repay are included in the form. Will my 1098T include payments I made during prior calendar year semesters? No, you do not receive credit on the 1098T form for prior calendar term payments made in the current term. If I made a payment for the current term in the previous year will I see it? Yes, it will appear on your previous year 1098T form because the payment was made in the current year. Why does my student ID not appear on my 1098T? ID numbers are not valid social security numbers so the government requires that we leave the box blank. Since I received 1098T form, am I qualified to receive one of the educational tax credits? If you received a 1098T form you are not automatically qualified to receive an educational tax credit. The determination of eligibility is the responsibility of the taxpayer. Can I claim both educational credits this year? No, you can only select one of the credits for any given tax year What is the Hunter College's Federal ID number?
